subject: Hospitality
title: Robot Servers and Automation
description: A quick, practical guide to Robot Servers and Automation.

hook.text: In Japan and China, robot servers deliver food to tables. They follow mapped routes, avoid obstacles, and never call in sick.

buildup.text: Robots like BellaBot and Servi handle food running and bussing—the repetitive tasks that burn out human staff fastest.

discovery.text: A single delivery robot costs $15,000–20,000. It replaces $30,000+ in annual labor for simple food running tasks.

twist.text: Guests have mixed reactions: novelty fades quickly, and many prefer human interaction.

climax.text: The ideal model is human-robot collaboration: robots handle carrying and clearing while humans handle empathy, selling.

punchline.text: Robots carry, humans connect. Automation works best where warmth isn't needed.

quiz.question: Where do robot servers work best in hospitality?
options: Repetitive tasks like food running and bussing—backstage more than front-stage
